full_judgment: 2. Their case, in short, is that, their predecessors and they themselves as co-sharers in the relevant khatians, mentioned in Ka, kha and Ga schedule to the plaint, got the suit land through different pre-emption cases, instituted under section 26F of the Bengal Tenancy Act, when their other co-sharers had sold the same on different dates to stranger purchasers and a few of them are also defendants in the present suit. In pursuance of the judgments and orders, passed in those pre-emption cases, they got possession in the suit land through Court and those purchasers thereby lost their right, title and interest in the suit jote. The superior landlord of Ga schedule land instituted Rent Suit No. 3534 of 1954 against the plaintiffs and some of the defendants. In that rent suit the plaintiffs compromised with the superior landlord on payment of arrears of rent, as claimed. After getting possession in the suit land the plaintiffs possessed the same for 5/6 years themselves and thereafter engaged defendant Nos. 1 and 2 as their borgadars in respect of RS plot Nos. 179 and 306. They also engaged defendant No. 4 and the predecessor of defendant Nos. 5-7 as borgadars in respect of RS plot Nos. 55, 79, 215, 298 and part of 297. Those borgadars had been delivering the borga crops to the plaintiffs for several years. But from Kartik 1382 BS, upon taking advantage of wrong recording of one Brajabanshi in the SA Khatian those borgadars stopped delivering of borga crops. The plaintiff also purchased the land of plot No. 307 of RS Khatian 34, mentioned in schedule Ka to the plaint by a registered kabala dated 11-6-60.
